claim: Kinetochores are the chromosomal attachment points for spindle microtubules.
source: Kinetochores are the chromosomal attachment points for spindle microtubules.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about kinetochore function.

claim: Kinetochores are signaling hubs that control major cell cycle transitions and coordinate chromosome folding.
source: They are also signaling hubs that control major cell cycle transitions and coordinate chromosome folding.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about kinetochore function.

claim: Most well-studied eukaryotes rely on a conserved set of factors for kinetochore functions.
source: Most well-studied eukaryotes rely on a conserved set of factors, which are divided among two loosely-defined groups, for these functions.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about kinetochore composition.

claim: Outer kinetochore proteins contact microtubules or regulate this contact directly.
source: Outer kinetochore proteins contact microtubules or regulate this contact directly.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about outer kinetochore protein function.

claim: Inner kinetochore proteins designate the kinetochore assembly site by recognizing a specialized nucleosome containing the H3 variant Cse4/CENP-A.
source: Inner kinetochore proteins designate the kinetochore assembly site by recognizing a specialized nucleosome containing the H3 variant Cse4/CENP-A.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about inner kinetochore protein function.

claim: The structure of the yeast Ctf19 complex was previously determined by cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM).
source: We previously determined the structure, resolved by cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), of the yeast Ctf19 complex (Ctf19c, homologous to the vertebrate CCAN), providing a high-resolution view of inner kinetochore architecture (Hinshaw and Harrison, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: The yeast Ctf19 complex is homologous to the vertebrate CCAN.
source: We previously determined the structure, resolved by cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), of the yeast Ctf19 complex (Ctf19c, homologous to the vertebrate CCAN), providing a high-resolution view of inner kinetochore architecture (Hinshaw and Harrison, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: A near-atomic model of the Ctf3 complex has been determined.
source: We now extend these observations by reporting a near-atomic model of the Ctf3 complex, the outermost Ctf19c sub-assembly seen in our original cryo-EM density.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the current study, supported by the cryo-EM data presented.

claim: The Ctf3 complex is the outermost Ctf19c sub-assembly.
source: We now extend these observations by reporting a near-atomic model of the Ctf3 complex, the outermost Ctf19c sub-assembly seen in our original cryo-EM density.
evidence: This is based on the previous cryo-EM structure of the full Ctf19c.

claim: The new Ctf3 complex model enables molecular interpretation of Ctf3 recruitment and function.
source: The model is sufficiently well-determined by the new data to enable molecular interpretation of Ctf3 recruitment and function.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the quality of the structural data obtained.

claim: Inner kinetochore proteins, particularly members of the Ctf19c, constitute the foundation of the kinetochore.
source: Inner kinetochore proteins, particularly members of the Ctf19c, constitute the foundation of the kinetochore; they both recognize Cse4/CENP-A and recruit microtubule-interacting outer kinetochore proteins (Musacchio and Desai, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: Ctf19c proteins both recognize Cse4/CENP-A and recruit microtubule-interacting outer kinetochore proteins.
source: Inner kinetochore proteins, particularly members of the Ctf19c, constitute the foundation of the kinetochore; they both recognize Cse4/CENP-A and recruit microtubule-interacting outer kinetochore proteins (Musacchio and Desai, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: Many Ctf19c factors were originally cloned and characterized for their contributions to faithful mitotic chromosome segregation.
source: Many of these factors were originally cloned and characterized for their contributions to faithful mitotic chromosome segregation (Hinshaw and Harrison, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: Specific Ctf19c activities that support chromosome segregation include specification of centromere-proximal origins as early-firing.
source: Specific Ctf19c activities that support chromosome segregation include specification of centromere-proximal origins as early-firing, recruitment of the Scc2/4 cohesin loading complex and its payload, the cohesin complex, and, as has been recently determined, recruitment of the chromosome passenger complex and its essential kinase subunit, Ipl1/Aurora B (Fernius et al., 2013; García-Rodríguez et al., 2019; Halwachs et al., 2018; Natsume et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: Specific Ctf19c activities that support chromosome segregation include recruitment of the Scc2/4 cohesin loading complex and its payload, the cohesin complex.
source: Specific Ctf19c activities that support chromosome segregation include specification of centromere-proximal origins as early-firing, recruitment of the Scc2/4 cohesin loading complex and its payload, the cohesin complex, and, as has been recently determined, recruitment of the chromosome passenger complex and its essential kinase subunit, Ipl1/Aurora B (Fernius et al., 2013; García-Rodríguez et al., 2019; Halwachs et al., 2018; Natsume et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: Specific Ctf19c activities that support chromosome segregation include recruitment of the chromosome passenger complex and its essential kinase subunit, Ipl1/Aurora B.
source: Specific Ctf19c activities that support chromosome segregation include specification of centromere-proximal origins as early-firing, recruitment of the Scc2/4 cohesin loading complex and its payload, the cohesin complex, and, as has been recently determined, recruitment of the chromosome passenger complex and its essential kinase subunit, Ipl1/Aurora B (Fernius et al., 2013; García-Rodríguez et al., 2019; Halwachs et al., 2018; Natsume et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: Recent findings suggest a handoff between Ctf19c-dependent microtubule contact points, whereby the link between centromeric DNA and spindle microtubules shifts between chromosomal tethers during the course of the cell cycle.
source: Recent findings also suggest a handoff between Ctf19c-dependent microtubule contact points, whereby the link between centromeric DNA and spindle microtubules shifts between chromosomal tethers during the course of the cell cycle (Bock et al., 2012; Hara et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Understanding coordination of diverse Ctf19c activities requires a structural picture of the inner kinetochore.
source: Understanding coordination of these diverse activities requires a structural picture of the inner kinetochore.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the need for structural information.

claim: Both Scc2/4 recruitment and stable microtubule binding at later stages of the cell cycle depend on the conserved Ctf3/CENP-I complex (Ctf3c).
source: Both Scc2/4 recruitment and stable microtubule binding at later stages of the cell cycle depend on the conserved Ctf3/CENP-I complex (Ctf3c) (Hara et al., 2018; Lang et al., 2018; Natsume et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: Ctf3 is a 733 amino-acid residue protein predicted to consist almost entirely of HEAT repeats.
source: The Ctf3c namesake, Ctf3, is a 733 amino-acid residue protein predicted to consist almost entirely of HEAT repeats (Huntingin, elongation factor 3 (EF3), protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A), and yeast kinase TOR1 repeats) (Basilico et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Ctf3 associates with a coiled-coil dimer of Mcm16 and Mcm22 (Mcm16/22).
source: Ctf3 associates with a coiled-coil dimer of Mcm16 and Mcm22 (Mcm16/22).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Ctf3 complex composition.

claim: The vertebrate Ctf3/CENP-I complex also includes the CENP-M protein, which has no known counterpart in yeast.
source: The vertebrate Ctf3/CENP-I complex also includes the CENP-M protein, which has no known counterpart in yeast (Basilico et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: The Mcm16/22 heterodimer can be purified from recombinant sources.
source: The Mcm16/22 heterodimer can be purified from recombinant sources, and the dimer is required for recovery of the full-length Ctf3 protein.
evidence: This is a statement about experimental observations.

claim: The Mcm16/22 dimer is required for recovery of the full-length Ctf3 protein.
source: The Mcm16/22 heterodimer can be purified from recombinant sources, and the dimer is required for recovery of the full-length Ctf3 protein.
evidence: This is a statement about experimental observations.

claim: Deletion of any one Ctf3 complex member perturbs recruitment of the other two to the kinetochore.
source: Deletion of any one complex member perturbs recruitment of the other two to the kinetochore, and the intact complex binds and recruits the Cnn1-Wip1 dimer, which connects to microtubules through the four-protein Ndc80 complex (Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: The intact Ctf3 complex binds and recruits the Cnn1-Wip1 dimer, which connects to microtubules through the four-protein Ndc80 complex.
source: Deletion of any one complex member perturbs recruitment of the other two to the kinetochore, and the intact complex binds and recruits the Cnn1-Wip1 dimer, which connects to microtubules through the four-protein Ndc80 complex (Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: In wild-type cells, kinetochore-localized Ctf3-GFP signal fluctuates throughout the cell cycle, appearing to peak in late anaphase before dropping as cells enter S phase.
source: In wild-type cells, kinetochore-localized Ctf3-GFP signal fluctuates throughout the cell cycle, appearing to peak in late anaphase before dropping as cells enter S phase (Pot et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: A high-resolution Ctf3c structure has not yet been reported prior to this study.
source: A high-resolution Ctf3c structure, which would enable molecular interpretation of the functions listed above, has yet to be reported.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field prior to the current work.

claim: Three-dimensional reconstructions of negatively-stained human CENP-I assemblies yielded an envelope for the complex consistent with the predicted HEAT repeat architecture for Ctf3/CENP-I, but the overall resolution was insufficient to support modeling beyond placement of putative domains.
source: Three-dimensional reconstructions of negatively-stained human CENP-I assemblies yielded an envelope for the complex consistent with the predicted HEAT repeat architecture for Ctf3/CENP-I, but the overall resolution was insufficient to support modeling beyond placement of putative domains (Basilico et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Recent X-ray crystal structures showed the HEAT repeat architecture of an N-terminal fragment of fungal Ctf3 (Ctf3-N) bound with C-terminal fragments of Mcm16 and Mcm22 (Mcm16/22 C), providing a model for this part of the Ctf3c.
source: Recent X-ray crystal structures showed the HEAT repeat architecture of an N-terminal fragment of fungal Ctf3 (Ctf3-N) bound with C-terminal fragments of Mcm16 and Mcm22 (Mcm16/22 C), providing a model for this part of the Ctf3c (Hu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: The previous cryo-EM reconstruction of the yeast Ctf19c enabled modeling of most of the ordered polypeptide chains, but the Ctf3c appeared flexibly attached to the core of the complex, limiting the apparent resolution for this region of the map and model.
source: Our previous cryo-EM reconstruction of the yeast Ctf19c enabled modeling of most of the ordered polypeptide chains, but the Ctf3c appeared flexibly attached to the core of the complex, limiting the apparent resolution for this region of the map and model (Hinshaw and Harrison, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: In the previous Ctf19c structure, the authors could not confidently assign a sequence register to the Ctf3 HEAT repeats or to the Mcm16/22 coiled-coil.
source: Consequently, we could not confidently assign a sequence register to the Ctf3 HEAT repeats we observed or to the Mcm16/22 coiled-coil.
evidence: This is a statement about limitations of the previous work.

claim: The current study presents a cryo-EM structure of the yeast Ctf3c, which resolves the overall organization of the complex, shows how Ctf3 binds Mcm16/22, and clarifies Ctf3c recruitment to the larger Ctf19c.
source: We now present a cryo-EM structure of the yeast Ctf3c, which resolves the overall organization of the complex, shows how Ctf3 binds Mcm16/22, and clarifies Ctf3c recruitment to the larger Ctf19c.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the current study.

claim: The Ctf3c was purified and its structure was determined by single-particle cryo-EM.
source: We purified the Ctf3c and determined its structure by single-particle cryo-EM (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Initial two-dimensional averages derived from a small hand-picked particle set matched projections of the density assigned to the Ctf3c in the full Ctf19c reconstruction (EMDB-0523).
source: Initial images yielded two-dimensional averages, derived from a small hand-picked particle set, that matched projections of the density assigned to the Ctf3c in the full Ctf19c reconstruction (EMDB-0523).
evidence: This describes experimental observations from the cryo-EM analysis.

claim: Additional blurry density was visible at the tips of several average particle images, likely indicating the presence of a domain (probably Ctf3-N and associated Mcm16/22 C) without a fixed orientation relative to the well-resolved features.
source: Additional blurry density was visible at the tips of several average particle images, likely indicating the presence of a domain (probably Ctf3-N and associated Mcm16/22 C, see below) without a fixed orientation relative to the well-resolved features.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cryo-EM data.

claim: Particles contributing to two-dimensional averages that showed fine features were used for calculation of an initial three-dimensional reconstruction.
source: Particles contributing to two-dimensional averages that showed fine features were used for calculation of an initial three-dimensional reconstruction.
evidence: This describes the data processing approach.

claim: Structural information from the previous Ctf19c reconstruction was not included at any stage of model generation or refinement, except for visual comparison of cryo-EM density.
source: Except for visual comparison of cryo-EM density, we did not include structural information from the previous Ctf19c reconstruction at any stage of model generation or refinement.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach to ensure independence of the new structure.

claim: The final map shows side-chain density throughout the particle, enabling modeling at near-atomic resolution.
source: The final map shows side-chain density throughout the particle, enabling modeling at near-atomic resolution (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the quality of the cryo-EM map obtained, with reference to a figure.

claim: The overall architecture of the Ctf3c agrees well with the features previously assigned to it in the Ctf19c reconstruction.
source: The overall architecture of the Ctf3c agrees well with the features previously assigned to it in our Ctf19c reconstruction (Hinshaw and Harrison, 2019) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a comparison between the current structure and the previous one, supported by citation and figure reference.

claim: Clearly-resolved side-chain density throughout the map allowed identification of the amino-acid sequence of the Ctf3 domain visualized and the corresponding fragments of Mcm16/22.
source: Clearly-resolved side-chain density throughout the map allowed us to identify the amino-acid sequence of the Ctf3 domain visualized here and the corresponding fragments of Mcm16/22 (Figure 2—figure supplements 1–2, Table 1).
evidence: This describes the quality of the map and what it enabled, with reference to figures and a table.

claim: Five Ctf3-C HEAT repeats were modeled, which have the overall fold of canonical HEAT arrays.
source: We modeled five Ctf3-C HEAT repeats (Figure 2B), which have the overall fold of canonical HEAT arrays (Perry and Kleckner, 2003).
evidence: This describes the structural modeling results, supported by citation and figure reference.

claim: Nearly 120 amino acid residues interrupt an imperfect sixth repeat at the C-terminal end of the modeled peptide chain, making a helical knob.
source: Nearly 120 amino acid residues interrupt an imperfect sixth repeat at the C-terminal end of the modeled peptide chain, making a helical knob.
evidence: This describes a structural feature observed in the model.

claim: An Mcm16/22 coiled-coil occupies the cleft formed by the concave surface of the HEAT array.
source: As we saw in the previous Ctf3c model, an Mcm16/22 coiled-coil occupies the cleft formed by the concave surface of the HEAT array.
evidence: This describes a structural feature observed in the model.

claim: The two main components of the structure, Ctf3-C and Mcm16/22 N, have opposite polarities.
source: The two main components of the structure, Ctf3-C and Mcm16/22 N, have opposite polarities; the central parts of Mcm16 and Mcm22 form a parallel coiled-coil that begins near the C-terminal end of the modeled Ctf3 polypeptide.
evidence: This describes a structural feature observed in the model.

claim: The central parts of Mcm16 and Mcm22 form a parallel coiled-coil that begins near the C-terminal end of the modeled Ctf3 polypeptide.
source: The two main components of the structure, Ctf3-C and Mcm16/22 N, have opposite polarities; the central parts of Mcm16 and Mcm22 form a parallel coiled-coil that begins near the C-terminal end of the modeled Ctf3 polypeptide.
evidence: This describes a structural feature observed in the model.

claim: The N-terminal parts of Mcm16 and Mcm22 form a set of four interdigitated helices that pack onto the convex side of the C-terminal part of the HEAT array and contact the helical knob.
source: The N-terminal parts of Mcm16 and Mcm22, form a set of four interdigitated helices that pack onto the convex side of the C-terminal part of the HEAT array and contact the helical knob.
evidence: This describes a structural feature observed in the model.

claim: Sequence conservation analysis suggested structural similarity between the N- and C-terminal parts of human CENP-I.
source: Sequence conservation analysis suggested structural similarity between the N- and C-terminal parts of human CENP-I (Basilico et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Ctf3/CENP-I has a tandem HEAT repeat architecture, the N-terminal part of which was resolved crystallographically (PDB 3Z07), and the C-terminal part was resolved in the current study.
source: Indeed, Ctf3/CENP-I has a tandem HEAT repeat architecture, the N-terminal part of which was resolved crystallographically (PDB 3Z07) (Hu et al., 2019), and the C-terminal part we have resolved here.
evidence: This integrates the current findings with previous crystallographic work, supported by citation.

claim: The cryo-EM densities for Ctf3 (EMDB-0523 and the current study) imply that the two sets of Ctf3 HEAT repeats do not have a fixed relative orientation.
source: Our cryo-EM densities for Ctf3 (EMDB-0523 and here) imply that the two sets of Ctf3 HEAT repeats do not have a fixed relative orientation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cryo-EM data.

claim: Only 7 and 12 amino acid residues for Mcm16 and Mcm22 (respectively) connect the ordered regions that coordinate the two Ctf3 globular domains.
source: Nevertheless, only 7 and 12 amino acid residues for Mcm16 and Mcm22 (respectively) connect the ordered regions that coordinate the two Ctf3 globular domains (Hu et al., 2019) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a structural observation supported by citation and figure reference.

claim: The structure determined in the current study (Ctf3-C-Mcm16/22 N) is essentially the precise complement of the Ctf3-N-Mcm16/22 C crystal structure.
source: The final model shows that the structure determined here (Ctf3-C-Mcm16/22 N) is essentially the precise complement of the Ctf3-N-Mcm16/22 C crystal structure (Hu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a comparison between the current structure and a previous crystal structure, supported by citation.

claim: The Mcm16/22 dimer extends without a major interruption along the Ctf3 HEAT repeats, forming two tightly but flexibly linked structural modules: Ctf3-N-Mcm16/22 C and Ctf3-C-Mcm16/22 N.
source: Therefore, the Mcm16/22 dimer extends without a major interruption along the Ctf3 HEAT repeats, forming two tightly but flexibly linked structural modules: Ctf3-N-Mcm16/22 C and Ctf3-C-Mcm16/22 N.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural data.

claim: Ctf3c recruitment to the kinetochore depends on interactions with other Ctf19c proteins.
source: Ctf3c recruitment to the kinetochore depends on interactions with other Ctf19c proteins (Measday et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Ctf3c recruitment depends on amino acid residues 1–95 of Mcm21 (Mcm21-N), a region of the peptide chain not visible in published crystal structures.
source: We previously found that Ctf3c recruitment depends on amino acid residues 1–95 of Mcm21 (Mcm21-N), a region of the peptide chain not visible in published crystal structures (Schmitzberger and Harrison, 2012; Schmitzberger et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The high-resolution Ctf3c map allowed identification of features in the previous Ctf19c cryo-EM map that are not visible in the current model and therefore must correspond to Ctf19c proteins not included in the current reconstruction.
source: The high-resolution Ctf3c map we report here allowed us to identify features in the previous Ctf19c cryo-EM map that are not visible in the current model and therefore must correspond to Ctf19c proteins not included in the current reconstruction.
evidence: This is a logical inference from comparing the two maps.

claim: A small helical fragment packs into the cleft between the convex surface of the Ctf3 HEAT array and the Mcm16/22 N-terminal helices in the Ctf19c map.
source: First, a small helical fragment packs into the cleft between the convex surface of the Ctf3 HEAT array and the Mcm16/22 N-terminal helices in the Ctf19c map (Figure 3A).
evidence: This describes a structural feature observed in the Ctf19c map, with reference to a figure.

claim: The small helical fragment in the Ctf19c map likely accommodates a presumed short helical motif in Mcm21-N (Mcm21-10-34).
source: This fragment likely accommodates a presumed short helical motif in Mcm21-N (Mcm21-10-34) (García-Rodríguez et al., 2019; Hinshaw and Harrison, 2019).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data, supported by citations.

claim: The Ctf3c map lacks density for an extended peptide that snakes along the solvent-exposed surface of the Mcm16/22 N-terminal helices.
source: Second, the Ctf3c map lacks density for an extended peptide that snakes along the solvent-exposed surface of the Mcm16/22 N-terminal helices.
evidence: This describes a difference between the Ctf3c map and the Ctf19c map.

claim: The extended peptide visible in the Ctf19c map emanates from the first resolved Mcm21 residue (at its N-terminus; Mcm21-Ser153) and likely connects through a loop not visualized in the Ctf19c map to the short helix.
source: This extended peptide emanates from the first resolved Mcm21 residue (at its N-terminus; Mcm21-Ser153) and likely connects through a loop not visualized in the Ctf19c map to the short helix mentioned above.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data.

claim: The new Ctf3c map enabled unambiguous identification of the Ctf3 residues that contact Iml3 and likely contribute to Ctf3c kinetochore recruitment.
source: The new Ctf3c map also enabled unambiguous identification of the Ctf3 residues that contact Iml3 and likely contribute to Ctf3c kinetochore recruitment.
evidence: This describes what the new map enabled in terms of identifying protein-protein interactions.

claim: Docking the new Ctf3c model determined at high resolution into the Ctf19c map shows that density for bulky Ctf3 residues can be accounted for by the new model.
source: Docking the new Ctf3c model determined at high resolution into the Ctf19c map shows that density for bulky Ctf3 residues can be accounted for by the new model (Figure 3B).
evidence: This describes the result of docking the new model into the previous map, with reference to a figure.

claim: Continuous density connecting Ctf3 and Iml3 accommodates Ctf3-Arg366, which packs onto Iml3-Trp112, likely enabling hydrophobic contact between the tryptophan indole and the aliphatic part of the arginine side chain.
source: Continuous density connecting Ctf3 and Iml3 accommodates Ctf3-Arg366, which packs onto Iml3-Trp112, likely enabling hydrophobic contact between the tryptophan indole and the aliphatic part of the arginine side chain.
evidence: This describes a specific protein-protein interaction observed in the structure.

claim: The neighboring Ctf3-Lys365 is well-positioned to make a salt bridge with Iml3-Glu82 in the full Ctf19c.
source: The neighboring Ctf3-Lys365 is well-positioned to make a salt bridge with Iml3-Glu82 in the full Ctf19c.
evidence: This describes a potential interaction based on the structural model.

claim: The ctf3-SDD allele (Ctf3-W362S,K365D,R366D) was created to test whether the Ctf3-Iml3 interface contributes to Ctf3c kinetochore recruitment.
source: To test whether this interface, like the one we previously reported between Ctf3 and Mcm21-N, contributes to Ctf3c kinetochore recruitment, we mutated three protruding residues to create the ctf3-SDD allele (Ctf3-W362S,K365D,R366D).
evidence: This describes the experimental design to test a hypothesis.

claim: Yeast cells expressing Mcm22-GFP and Ctf3-WT display Mcm22-GFP localization that matches that of Ctf3-GFP.
source: Yeast cells expressing Mcm22-GFP (to mark Ctf3c localization), Spc110-mCherry (to mark the spindle pole body/kinetochore), and Ctf3-WT display Mcm22-GFP localization that matches that of Ctf3-GFP (Hinshaw and Harrison, 2019).
evidence: This describes experimental observations, supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Cells lacking Iml3 (iml3Δ) or expressing the ctf3-SDD allele showed defective Mcm22-GFP localization.
source: Cells lacking Iml3 (iml3Δ) or expressing the ctf3-SDD allele showed defective Mcm22-GFP localization, a phenotype that was less severe in ctf3-SDD cells than in iml3Δ cells but was reproducible in three independently-derived ctf3-SDD strains (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes experimental results, with reference to figures.

claim: The defective Mcm22-GFP localization phenotype was less severe in ctf3-SDD cells than in iml3Δ cells but was reproducible in three independently-derived ctf3-SDD strains.
source: Cells lacking Iml3 (iml3Δ) or expressing the ctf3-SDD allele showed defective Mcm22-GFP localization, a phenotype that was less severe in ctf3-SDD cells than in iml3Δ cells but was reproducible in three independently-derived ctf3-SDD strains (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes experimental results, with reference to figures.

claim: The Iml3-Ctf3 interface observed in cryo-EM reconstructions of the full Ctf19c recapitulates the one used by cells to recruit the Ctf3c to the kinetochore.
source: Therefore, the Iml3-Ctf3 interface we observe in cryo-EM reconstructions of the full Ctf19c recapitulates the one used by cells to recruit the Ctf3c to the kinetochore.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: There are three published Ctf3c/CENP-I complex models.
source: There are three published Ctf3c/CENP-I complex models (Basilico et al., 2014; Hinshaw and Harrison, 2019; Hu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field, supported by citations.

claim: The volume derived from a negative-stain electron microscopy reconstruction of the four-protein human CENP-I complex (CENP-H/I/K/M) could likely accommodate the model presented in the current study, along with the N-terminal part of the Ctf3/CENP-I and human CENP-M.
source: The volume derived from a negative-stain electron microscopy reconstruction of the four-protein human CENP-I complex (CENP-H/I/K/M) could likely accommodate the model we present here, along with the N-terminal part of the Ctf3/CENP-I and human CENP-M.
evidence: This is a comparison between the current model and a previous negative-stain EM reconstruction.

claim: The recent Ctf3c structure determined in the context of the full Ctf19c provides information about the mechanism of Ctf3c recruitment but did not allow confident assignment of amino acid sequence to the density.
source: Our recent Ctf3c structure, which we determined in the context of the full Ctf19c, provides information about the mechanism of Ctf3c recruitment but did not allow us to confidently assign amino acid sequence to the density.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the previous work.

claim: A recent crystal structure of Ctf3 from Chaetomium thermophilum in complex with Mcm16/22 from a related species (Thielavia terrestri) provides a high-resolution view of the Ctf3/CENP-I N-terminal domain and of the Mcm16/22 C-terminal regions but no information about the domains reported in the current study.
source: Finally, a recent crystal structure of Ctf3 from Chaetomium thermophilum in complex with Mcm16/22 from a related species (Thielavia terrestri) provides a high-resolution view of the Ctf3/CENP-I N-terminal domain and of the Mcm16/22 C-terminal regions but no information about the domains we report here.
evidence: This is a comparison between the current work and a previous crystal structure.

claim: Incorporation of the updated Ctf3c model into the previous model of the Ctf19c yields a nearly complete structural description of this 13-protein kinetochore anchor.
source: Incorporation of the updated Ctf3c model into our previous model of the Ctf19c yields a nearly complete structural description of this 13-protein kinetochore anchor (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a conclusion about the completeness of the structural model, with reference to a figure.

claim: Newly-resolved interfaces between Ctf3 and the Ctf19c proteins Iml3 and Mcm21 enable direct visualization and modulation of Ctf3c recruitment.
source: Newly-resolved interfaces between Ctf3 and the Ctf19c proteins Iml3 and Mcm21 enable direct visualization and, consequently, modulation of Ctf3c recruitment.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the implications of the structural findings.

claim: A more precise understanding of Ctf3c recruitment will need to account for dynamic localization of Ctf3 and its binding partner Cnn1 during the cell cycle.
source: A more precise understanding of Ctf3c recruitment will need to account for dynamic localization of Ctf3 and its binding partner Cnn1 during the cell cycle.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: Post-translational modification of Ctf3c proteins, Cnn1, Mcm21, Mif2/CENP-C, or some combination of these factors may explain the dynamic localization behavior of Ctf3.
